description: USE THIS for "where can I get water", "is there a spring, creek, lake or waterfall near", "hot springs near" or "where do I fill up" at a latitude and longitude in Montana's Custer Gallatin, Beaverhead-Deerlodge, Lolo, Kootenai, Flathead, Bitterroot and Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forests and the Montana part of the Idaho Panhandle, any Oregon National Forest, or public land in Arizona and Utah (national forests, Bureau of Land Management field offices and state land with public access). Returns up to 25 water records within a straight-line radius (up to 50 miles), nearest first: springs, hot springs, waterfalls, lakes, reservoirs, rivers, creeks and fill points, each with its kind, straight-line miles, what the record says about drinking in plain words (it never calls water drinkable: always filter or boil), how access is recorded (a road or trail record, not a condition), elevation, season, any posted advisory (a record with an advisory never says filter or boil: read the advisory), the source links with the record date, and what the record does not hold. In Arizona and Utah each record also says whether the record marks it as water all year, dry part of the year, or does not say it holds water: a mapped point in the desert is not a promise of water, so say the recorded words and tell the person to carry their water. A point outside that area answers with an empty list and says so; it never guesses. The land manager office has the final word.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (negative in the US).

types.description: Keep only these kinds of water.

name: water_near
title: Water near a point (Montana, Oregon, Arizona and Utah public land)
